chats.answer:
For a 15–16-inch triple-screen laptop extender with 1920 × 1200 resolution (16:10), I'd focus on models that add two independent displays to your existing laptop screen.

The distinction matters: many extenders advertised as “15.6-inch FHD” are only 1920 × 1080. I filtered those out.

Best options I found
Best overall candidate

MagHub Trio Go 16" Portable Screen Extender

$549 sale listing

Dual 16" IPS, 1920 × 1200, 100% sRGB, 60Hz. One-cable setup with a required driver. Good option for productivity and a relatively simple connection.

4.6/5 · 125 merchant reviews

APILDELLA 16" Triple Laptop Screen Extender, 1200P 16:10 Por…

$432.99

Dual 16" 1920 × 1200, 16:10, slim design, approximately 4 lb. A more affordable travel-oriented option with USB-C/HDMI connectivity.

Closest to 15 inches

NGTeco 15.3 Inch Triple Screen Extender for Laptop, 1200P Po…

$351.99

15.3" 1200P model, advertised at just 2.64 lb with an H5-T adapter. Attractive for portability, although the listing has limited review evidence.

Hyangin Triple Screen Laptop Monitor Extender 15.6", 2026 Up…

$582.99

Three integrated 15.6" 1920 × 1200 IPS panels, rather than just two added screens. 300 nits and 100% sRGB advertised. Much heavier, at approximately 7.6 lb.

These are manufacturer or retailer specifications, not independently verified measurements. In particular, I'd confirm the NGTeco's exact native resolution before buying.

My preference is the INVZI if you want two additional 16:10 screens and don't mind installing a driver. If you need exactly 15-inch-class displays, the NGTeco is worth investigating first.

One important compatibility issue: not every laptop can run two additional independent monitors natively, particularly some base-model Apple Silicon MacBooks.

One question before I narrow it down

Which laptop are you using (exact model and chip/processor)? That will determine which extender can actually run both additional screens, whether it needs a driver, and which is the best purchase for your setup.

chats.answer:
For a 15–16-inch triple-screen laptop extender with 1920×1200 (16:10) displays, my top pick is the FOPO S9G for value, or the FOPO S11 for a more conventional attached setup.

There are two interpretations of "triple": two added screens plus your laptop (three total), or three added screens (four total). Here are the strongest options for both.

Best options compared

1. FOPO S9G

Best value
$299.99

Two 16-inch 1920×1200 IPS screens, detachable design, 60Hz. Native video connection without a display driver, assuming compatible laptop outputs.

2 added screens · 16:10 · approximately 2.4 kg

FOPO official store

2. FOPO S11

Best conventional setup
$399.99

Two 16-inch 1920×1200 IPS panels, 300-nit advertised brightness, native USB-C or HDMI video, no driver required.

2 added screens · 16:10 · approximately 2 kg

FOPO official store

3. Hyangin Z3

Exact 15.6-inch match

Three 15.6-inch 1920×1200 IPS panels, advertised 300 nits and 100% sRGB. Heavier at 3.45 kg, but provides three additional displays.

3 added screens · 16:10 · 60Hz

View on Newegg

4. FOPO S788

$499.99

Three 16-inch 1920×1200 IPS panels, 100% sRGB advertised. Single USB connection with driver installation and external power.

3 added screens · 16:10 · 2.64 kg

View at FOPO

Prices are observed listings, not guaranteed checkout prices. Specifications are manufacturer-advertised; these are not hands-on test rankings. 
Dealectric
+3
What I would choose

Two extra screens: FOPO S9G, particularly for Windows laptops with two video-capable outputs.

Three extra screens: FOPO S788, for its lighter weight and lower listed price compared with several alternatives.

Strictly 15.6-inch panels: Hyangin Z3, although it is substantially heavier.

One important detail: many USB-C extenders require DisplayPort Alt Mode, while driver-based models can support different laptop configurations. MacBook compatibility also varies by chip.

Two questions to narrow this down:

How many additional screens do you want?

2 additional screens (3 total including laptop)
3 additional screens (4 total including laptop)

What laptop are you using?

MacBook
Windows laptop
